chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir said:

I asked one of the two of them (peace be upon them) about buying the khums of the al-khiyanah and al-sariqah. He said: 'There is no (khums) except if another share has mixed with it. As for the sariqah itself, there is no (khums) except if it is from the property of the Sultan, then there is no harm with that.'

key_terms.الْخِيَانَةِ: Al-khiyanah, a specific type of wealth or treasure subject to khums
key_terms.اِخْتَلَطَ: Mixed (referring to the mixing of wealth shares)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of khums on al-khiyanah and al-sariqah?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction is drawn between *al-khiyanah* (often interpreted as hidden treasure or *kanz*) and *al-sariqah* (plunder/booty), clarifying that khums is generally not due on the former unless mixed with other wealth, but is obligatory on the latter if it originates from the Sultan's property. This ruling highlights the unique fiscal status of the Imam's share in state spoils within Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from general private wealth. The condition of mixing (*ikhtilat*) serves as a practical mechanism for determining liability when ownership becomes indistinguishable.
